title: Dust control: extraction, wet cleaning and safe clean-up
audience: Timber floor restoration workers who set up and run sanding, screening and clean-up.
learningOutcomes: Set up extraction at each dust source before sanding starts.
Choose a wet or HEPA clean-up method and explain why dry sweeping and compressed air are not used.
Record the extraction check and the waste disposal for each room.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: WorkSafe Victoria, Wood dust: health hazards and control (reviewed 17/04/2026); SafeWork NSW, Wood dust: health hazards and control (wood safety kit) (published 20 Sep 2018; last modified 11 July 2023, page metadata).

instruction.heading: The control order for sanding dust
instruction.body: WorkSafe Victoria (reviewed 17/04/2026) sets out an order of controls: eliminate first, then substitution, isolation and engineering controls, then administrative controls, with PPE last. For sanding an installed floor, the practical controls are to isolate the work area, to substitute a lower-dust method or product where one is approved, and then to use engineering controls, mainly local exhaust ventilation at each dust source. Administrative controls and PPE come only after those, for the risk that remains.

instruction.heading: Extraction at the source
instruction.body: Local exhaust ventilation should capture dust as close as possible to each dust source, and every dust source on a machine should be controlled. Portable tools should use on-tool extraction connected to a dust collector, with a minimum recommendation of Dust Class M. WorkSafe Victoria notes that dust bags on portable tools alone do not capture fine dust efficiently. Inspect the extraction before each job, and check hoses and ducts for holes and leaks.

instruction.heading: Clean-up with wet methods and HEPA
instruction.body: Use wet cleaning methods such as mopping and wiping, and damp down surfaces before sweeping, as WorkSafe Victoria recommends; SafeWork NSW's wood dust page (last modified 11 July 2023) gives the same advice. Dry sweeping is listed by WorkSafe Victoria as an activity that generates airborne wood dust, and it is not presented as an acceptable method. Use an industrial vacuum with a HEPA filter, also rated at least Dust Class M, for dust that remains. Use the same approach for dust on clothing and equipment.

instruction.heading: Never use compressed air
instruction.body: Compressed air must not be used to clear workbenches, and it must not be used to blow dust off skin or clothing. WorkSafe Victoria (reviewed 17/04/2026) says compressed air re-suspends dust and poses an eye injury risk, and that on skin or clothing it can push air into the circulation, with serious effects including death. A HEPA vacuum is the method to use for clothing.

instruction.heading: Keep dust in the room where it is made
instruction.body: Seal the work area with plastic and tape, close doors to adjoining rooms, and keep occupants and pets out. Keep the sanding sequence moving so dust is removed at the machine rather than left in the room. Dust from the job must be bagged and labelled according to the approved waste procedure, not left loose in the room or placed in ordinary household bins without approval.

procedure: Seal the work area and close doors to adjoining rooms and occupied spaces.
Connect on-tool extraction to a dust collector and HEPA vacuum rated at least Dust Class M.
Check that the extraction is working and that there are no leaks before sanding starts.
Sand in an order that keeps dust at the machine, and stop to clear accumulated dust in the work area.
Damp down surfaces before any sweeping. Use wet cleaning and a HEPA vacuum for clean-up.
Do not use compressed air on the floor, benches or skin. Use a HEPA vacuum on clothing.
Bag and label dust and waste according to the approved procedure, and record the controls used.

workedExamples.situation: A sander with only its dust bag attached is being used in a bedroom. The doorway to the living area is open, and a family is at home. At the end of the shift the worker plans to sweep the floor dry.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must change before work continues, and what is the correct clean-up?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the work. A dust bag alone does not capture fine dust, so connect the sander to HEPA extraction rated at least Dust Class M, seal the doorway, and keep the family out of the area. Do not dry-sweep. Damp down the surfaces and use a wet clean and a HEPA vacuum. Bag the waste according to the procedure and record the controls and the extraction check.

equipmentAndPpe: On-tool extraction connected to a dust collector, rated at least Dust Class M
Industrial HEPA vacuum rated at least Dust Class M
Plastic sheeting and tape for sealing
Damp mops, wet wipes and labelled waste bags

commonErrors.error: Relying on a dust bag on a portable sander.
commonErrors.prevention: Connect the tool to HEPA extraction rated at least Dust Class M.

commonErrors.error: Dry sweeping at the end of the day.
commonErrors.prevention: Damp down, then use a wet clean and a HEPA vacuum.

commonErrors.error: Using compressed air to clear dust from clothes or benches.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a HEPA vacuum. Never use compressed air.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the extraction unchecked after the first hour.
commonErrors.prevention: Check extraction at the start of the job, and again after any change of machine or room.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: WorkSafe Victoria (page reviewed 17/04/2026) advises against using compressed air on benches, skin or clothing, and reports serious effects including death when it is used on skin.

qualityStandard: Extraction is connected and working before sanding starts, and the check is recorded.
No dry sweeping and no compressed air are used at any point.
Clean-up is completed with damp methods and a HEPA vacuum, and the waste is bagged and labelled.
documentationEvidence: Extraction and vacuum equipment check record, with date and room
Dust control record for each room
Waste disposal record following the approved procedure
summary: Capture dust at the source with extraction rated at least Dust Class M.
Clean with damp methods and a HEPA vacuum. Never dry-sweep.
Never use compressed air on a floor, a bench, skin or clothing.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: WorkSafe Victoria, Wood dust: health hazards and control (reviewed 17/04/2026); SafeWork NSW, Wood dust: health hazards and control (wood safety kit) (published 20 Sep 2018; last modified 11 July 2023, page metadata).

knowledgeChecks.question: What does WorkSafe Victoria recommend for portable sanders?
options: On-tool extraction connected to a collector rated at least Dust Class M
A dust bag alone on the sander, the tool body, the cord and the hose
Open windows only and no extraction at all on the job site
A fan blowing the dust out of the room, the house and the yard

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is dry sweeping of wood dust a problem?
options: It makes floors too smooth and slippery
It can generate airborne wood dust
It removes all the finish from the floor
Regulators require it on every job

knowledgeChecks.question: Which method is correct for clearing dust from clothing?
options: Compressed air
A dry brush
A HEPA vacuum
Shake them out

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen before sweeping?
options: Turn on a floor fan
Sweep straight away
Spray with a solvent
Damp down the surface

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about local exhaust ventilation is correct?
options: Capture dust close to each source and inspect it regularly
Set it up once and never check it again on any job
Use it only in the hallway of the house and the stairs
Replace it with a dust bag on the tool and the sander
